body:
### Describe your issue

Originally, there were two call nodes:
- `SimpleCallNode` for C function calls and Python calls with only positional arguments
- `GeneralCallNode` for all other Python function calls

Eventually new call nodes came into being to accommodate various call optimisations: unpacking methods and calling the unbound method, vectorcalls, inlined function calls, …

The call node landscape is historically grown and does not match what the today's Python call interfaces look like. This is worth cleaning up because it requires cross-cutting changes for many optimisations.

There should be the following nodes:
- `CFuncCallNode` – for C/C++ functions with signatures known at compile time. This can generate direct C function calls. This node will not originate from the parser but will be created from other call nodes during type analysis when it turns out that the callable is a C/C++ callable. There should be a way to instantiate it from a call with keyword arguments that it can map to the positional arguments of the call signature.
- `SimplePythonCallNode` – for simple Python calls with an explicit list of positional and (optionally) keyword arguments known at compile time. This can use the vectorcall interface to efficiently pass the arguments as args/kwargs vectors. It can employ further optimisations for certain special callables such as classes that instantiate a type, and it can try to map keyword arguments to positional arguments if the call signature is known at compile time.
- `PythonMethodCallNode` – for Python methods with an explicit list of positional and (optionally) keyword arguments known at compile time. It can use method vectorcalls. It will probably not be created by the parser but after constant folding when we know whether the keyword dict is constant or dynamically generated, and whether it's worth trying a method call and not a simple call to a `module.function()` etc.
- `GeneralPythonCallNode` – for Python calls with dynamically generated positional tuple and/or keyword dict arguments that are not known at compile time.

The following optimised call nodes might also be worth keeping:
- `CachedBuiltinMethodCallNode`
- `PythonCapiCallNode` (although it might also be wrapped into `CFuncCallNode` with a suitable constructor factory method for instantiation)
- `InlinedDefNodeCallNode` can probably be wrapped into `CFuncCallNode` with a suitable constructor factory
title: Refactor call nodes
